entries.test: Published evaluations of whether dominant neural-network models' reasoning and planning failures are concentrated on out-of-distribution inputs, compared with in-distribution ones.
entries.note: This is a mechanism claim that researchers still argue about, but the test is clear enough to grade.
The claim that a technical limit drives developers' ethical choices depends on their private motives. The data-greed half alone could be argued, but the claim as a whole turns on intent.
He never says what the data would need to be enough for, and 'always outliers' is close to true by definition. Readers would not agree on a test.

entries.test: Whether any LLM shows sustained, independently verified reliability (for example, error rates low enough for unsupervised use in high-stakes settings) on broad real-world tasks.
entries.note: The driverless-cars half of the sentence was left out and could be a separate observation. Because the claim says 'never', it can be refuted but not confirmed.

entries.test: Whether a system widely accepted as AGI is reached by scaling current architectures without new approaches that generalize better beyond their training data.
entries.note: How to define AGI is disputed, but the claim is firm about what AGI requires. Only a decisive event, such as AGI arriving through pure scaling, could settle it.
